correctness.rationale: For interior t, the 48 vertices are explicit and signed-permutation transitive. A direct 4x4 integer-polynomial determinant enumeration checks 178,365 anchored vertex quadruples, with 258 sign-normalized polynomial profiles and total multiplicity 178,365. Exactly 1,032 Q(sqrt(2)) Bernstein expansions (5 coefficients each) are coefficientwise nonnegative on [0,sqrt(2)-1] and [sqrt(2)-1,1/2]. The two displayed witness profiles attain the piecewise maximum, and exact quadratic-field comparison and factorization identify the unique interior crossover. Independent rational 4x4 determinants replay all 258 representative polynomials at t=1/3. Orbit and four-face incidence checks show 192 rigid left-side simplices and 48 matching edges of right-side maximizers (96 endpoint simplices), with same signed determinants on each movable-apex edge. Multiaffine equality expansion proves there are no other nonvertex maximizers in the open phases. The transition nonvertex locus is explicitly not fully classified; volume ratio follows by disjoint tip removal. The finite checks are exact and the proof extends them to all real t.

The full texts of the 2014 spherical-polytope and maximal-simplex complexity papers address respectively unconstrained spherical point sets and general approximation/hardness, neither the exact four-dimensional continuous truncation envelope nor its optimizer rigidity transition. value.rationale: The natural truncation path joins the 16-cell, Archimedean truncated 16-cell and 24-cell, while the maximal contained simplex is a recognized geometric approximation invariant. Beyond endpoint data, the exact sharp two-polynomial envelope has a nontrivial algebraic transition sqrt(2)-1 and a qualitative change from 192 isolated maximizers to 48 continuous families. Its parameter-uniform bound and precise uniform-polytope value 1/27 (9/154 occupancy) can serve as test cases for geometric and algorithmic simplex-approximation questions. It is more than a parameter substitution or numeric finite census: the continuous bound and equality structure have rigorous algebraic certificates.
